title: Bay St. Louis carnival parades and dances
summary: Labat describes the local carnival with its parade, street and hall dances, and the milder masking compared with New Orleans Indians.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I was on the own carnival.
What kind of carnival do you have over here?
Well, they have a parade, and right after the parade they have a dance until five o'clock that afternoon, then they resume that night from eight to twelve.
Do they dance in the streets or in the hall? Oh yeah, dance in the streets, in the hall too.
Dance anywhere on the carnival. That's where I can't do it. Yeah, real nice one.

Last carnival we had Indians. I mean they had some beautiful costumes. Yeah, costumes but... Not like the New Orleans Indians, though. Oh, nothing. Oh no. They're wild. They go wild. Yeah, we got tame Indians. They're supposed to get juiced over their ass. I don't have two pistols in their bosom. One, two. That's true. I'm afraid of them. One of my favorite Indian tribes, the chief had one on each side. He made these suits. Of course, every night when you come from work, you wait an hour and a half, two hours on your suit. Every year you have a different suit. They have beautiful suits. Yeah, who was playing with us when... When... I wanted to ask you something and you messed up. Excuse me. It's gone. It's gone. We'll get back to... Yeah, you might think of it while you're talking. While we're talking about it. I've been playing with so many fellas out in New Orleans. Well, who did you hear when you went over there in your younger days when you were just a little bitty boy? Did you go over and hear music then? In New Orleans?
